newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Wednesday on a lack of fresh market-moving stimuli, traders said.

The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract plunged to 8.0 percent from 15.0 percent last Friday on a technical correction after surges in the last few trading days before a four-day holiday, they said.
The market was closed from Saturday to Tuesday to mark the Chinese takeover of Hong Kong.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 3.8 million lots from 2.4 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the market was directionless on the absence of market-moving news after the long holiday.

"A lack of fresh stimuli made many investors reluctant to trade on the market," one trader said. "Only profit-taking by big institutions pulled down the early-maturing contracts, particularly the seven-day contract."
Traders said they expected repo rates to move around the current level in the next few days.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Wednesday partly because a fall on the stock markets pushed liquidity back to the spot market, traders said.
The most actively traded seven-year treasury note that matures in November 2003 rose to 96.15 yuan from 96.10 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose slightly to 494,869 lots from an extremely thin 471,021 lots.
Traders said thin volume indicated sentiment was still weak after the contracts had been on a downtrend for weeks.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to move narrowly around the current level in the next few days.
